questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 17 cm and a height of 10 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
questions.why: ½ × 17 × 10 = 85 cm². Say the formula first, then multiply, so you never forget to halve.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In a sealed container, 35g of reactants react completely. What is the mass of the products?
questions.why: Mass is conserved in a closed system — nothing can escape, so products equal 35g, same as the reactants.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do we call the solid that can suddenly appear when two liquids react?
questions.why: A precipitate is a solid that forms when two solutions react — its sudden appearance is a sign a new substance was made.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: A soft drink ad shows a famous swimmer celebrating with the product. What technique is this?
questions.why: Using a famous athlete to promote a product is celebrity endorsement — it makes the drink feel desirable even if it isn't healthy.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: On a nutrition label, what unit is the energy value usually shown in?
questions.why: Energy on a nutrition label is measured in kilojoules (kJ), not grams — grams measure the mass of nutrients like fat or sugar.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What is it called when heat is given off during a chemical reaction?
questions.why: A reaction that releases heat and feels warm is called exothermic — temperature change is another clear sign a new substance has formed.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: What does the energy value on a nutrition label tell you?
questions.why: The energy value shows how much energy (in kilojoules) is in a serving of the food — it's not about weight, ingredient count, or freshness.
